chunks: There will be a veil between them, and on the wall will be the men (of al-A'raf) who will recognise everyone by their distinguishing marks, and will call to the inmates of Paradise: "Peace on you," without having entered it themselves though hoping to do so.

key_terms.الْأَعْرَافِ: The Heights (a place between Paradise and Hell)

ai.seo_question: Who are the people of Al-A'raf and what is their status between Paradise and Hell?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the 'people of Al-A'raf' are often interpreted as those whose good and bad deeds were equal, placing them in a state of waiting (Barzakh) before final entry into Paradise. Their recognition of both groups by their 'seals' (sima) highlights the clarity of divine judgment, while their call of 'Salam' reflects their intermediate status—neither condemned nor yet fully admitted. This verse underscores the concept of divine justice where merit is precisely weighed, a key theme in Shia theology regarding the afterlife.
